property_summary: The owner() function must return the actual owner address, not address(0). Since the bug makes owner() always return address(0), a new deployment will have its initial owner set to address(0) instead of the deployer, breaking the invariant that owner() equals the deployer after construction.

owner() must return the address that was set as _owner in Ownable's constructor (i.e., the deployer), but the mutant always returns address(0), so after a transferOwnership to a non-zero newOwner, owner() should reflect the new owner but instead remains zero.
After transferring ownership to a non-zero address, owner() must return that new owner, but the mutant always returns address(0).

For any address returned by owner(), it must match the address that deployed C or the address set by the onlyOwner transferOwnership call; the bug makes owner() always return address(0), violating this rule.

owner() must return the address that Ownable's _transferOwnership set as _owner, but the mutant always returns address(0) when a non-zero previous owner renounces ownership via renounceOwnership(), violating the invariant that a call to renounceOwnership() sets owner() to address(0) iff the previous owner was non-zero and the call was made by that previous owner.

The owner() function must always return the same address regardless of msg.sender; the bug makes owner() return msg.sender instead, so two different callers will see different owner() values when they should see the same stored owner.
For any two different callers, the owner() function must return the same address; the bug makes owner() return msg.sender, so different callers see different owner addresses.
Owner must remain constant across all callers; the bug makes owner() return msg.sender, so two different callers see different owner values.
The owner() function must return the same address for all callers; the bug makes it return msg.sender, so different callers will get different results.
The return value of owner() must be independent of the caller; the bug makes it return msg.sender, so the result changes when called by a different account.
The owner() return value must equal the stored owner, not msg.sender, so a non-owner can call owner() and get a false return; the buggy version returns msg.sender instead.

For any caller, owner() must return the address set by the constructor, not the caller's own address; the mutant returns msg.sender instead, so a non-owner caller can make owner() return a value different from the stored owner.

For any caller that is not the actual owner, owner() must return the address set in Ownable's constructor (_owner) and not msg.sender; the mutant returns msg.sender, so a non-owner caller receives their own address instead of the true owner.

For any caller, c.owner() must return the same address as the address that deployed the contract (set in the constructor) and not the caller's own address; the mutant returns msg.sender instead, so a non-owner caller can make owner() return their own address instead of the stored owner.

For any caller, c.owner() must return the address set during Ownable's constructor and not msg.sender; the mutant returns msg.sender, so a non-owner caller receives their own address, which differs from the stored owner.
The onlyOwner modifier should prevent non-owners from changing the owner via transferOwnership; the bug removes this restriction, allowing anyone to call transferOwnership and change the owner.
For any non-owner caller, transferOwnership must revert; the bug removes the onlyOwner check, allowing a non-owner to successfully change the owner.
After any call to transferOwnership from a non-owner, the owner must remain unchanged; the buggy modifier allows a non-owner to change the owner.

For any caller, if a call to transferOwnership changes the owner to a new non-zero address, the caller must be the current owner; the bug removes the onlyOwner check, allowing any non-owner caller to successfully change the owner.

After any call to transferOwnership(newOwner) where newOwner is non-zero, if the call does not revert then the new owner must equal the msg.sender of the call; the buggy onlyOwner modifier allows any caller to successfully transfer ownership to any address.

The owner can always transfer ownership to any non-zero address, but never to the zero address; the buggy version allows transferring ownership to the zero address, effectively renouncing ownership with a different function.
After any call to transferOwnership, the owner() must never be address(0); the buggy version breaks this by allowing a transfer to address(0).
After calling transferOwnership with any address, if the call does not revert, owner() must return a non-zero address; the buggy version allows transferring to address(0), making owner() return zero.
After a call to transferOwnership with the zero address, the correct contract reverts, while the buggy version does not revert and sets the owner to address(0).

For any input newOwner, if transferOwnership(newOwner) does not revert, then owner() must not be address(0); the buggy version removes the zero-address check, allowing a non-reverting transfer to address(0) which makes owner() == address(0).
Only the original owner can successfully transfer ownership; the bugged contract allows any non-owner to transfer ownership.
After any call to transferOwnership by a non-owner (here fuzzed address), the reference owner remains unchanged, but the buggy version changes owner to the input address.

In the reference contract, only the current owner can change _owner via transferOwnership; in the buggy version, after a non-owner calls transferOwnership with a non-zero address, the new owner is set to that address, which means the original owner can be replaced by anyone.
In the reference contract, after a non-owner calls transferOwnership, the owner remains unchanged; in the buggy version, the owner changes to the argument address.

After a non-owner calls transferOwnership, calling owner() must return the address that previously owned() before the call; the buggy contract violates this because it allows anyone to change the owner.
Only the current owner can change the operator, so after any call to setOperator by a non-owner, the operator remains unchanged in the reference but changes in the buggy version.
After any setOperator call, the operator must equal the previous owner if the caller was not the owner; the bug allows a non-owner to change it.
For any caller other than the owner, a call to setOperator must leave the operator unchanged from its initial value; the buggy version allows a non-owner to alter it.
After a non-owner calls setOperator(newOp), the operator remains equal to the original operator set during construction in the correct contract; the bug allows it to change.
After a non-owner calls setOperator(newOp), the operator must remain equal to the original operator set during construction; the buggy version allows a non-owner to change it to newOp.
After setOperator is called by any non-zero address, the operator state variable must equal the _operator argument passed, but the bug sets it to msg.sender instead.
After a non-owner calls setOperator with any argument, the operator state variable must remain unchanged, but the bug incorrectly updates it to the caller.
After any call to setOperator by the owner, the operator MUST equal the passed _operator argument; the bug sets it to msg.sender instead.
After the owner calls setOperator with any argument, the operator must equal the argument; the bug sets operator to msg.sender (the owner) instead.
After the owner calls setOperator, the operator must equal the _operator argument, but the bug sets it to msg.sender.
On the reference C, the rewardsRecipient state variable always equals the address passed to setRewardsRecipient; on the buggy version, rewardsRecipient remains unchanged after the call.
For any address A, after a successful call to setRewardsRecipient(A) by the owner, c.rewardsRecipient() must equal A; the buggy version always returns the zero address instead.
After the owner calls setRewardsRecipient with a non-zero address, the rewardsRecipient must equal that address; the bug leaves it unchanged.

After an owner call to setRewardsRecipient with any address A, the public getter rewardsRecipient() must equal A on the reference but remains unchanged (the value before the call) on the buggy version.

After the owner successfully calls setRewardsRecipient, the public getter rewardsRecipient() must return the address passed to the function. The buggy contract leaves it unchanged, so the getter does not equal the new address.
After any call to setRewardsRecipient, the rewardsRecipient state variable must equal the parameter passed.

After setRewardsRecipient is called, the emitted event’s recipient parameter must match the stored rewardsRecipient (the reference always does; the buggy version emits the argument but sets rewardsRecipient to address(0), so the storage will not match the event parameter for any non-zero argument).
After any call to setRewardsRecipient, the getReward function must transfer reward tokens to the new rewardsRecipient; the bug sets it to address(0), preventing transfers.

For any call to setRewardsRecipient with a non-zero address, a subsequent call to getReward when there are non-zero reward token balances must transfer all those balances to that address; the bug sets rewardsRecipient to address(0) preventing any transfer.

For any call to setRewardsRecipient, the address stored in rewardsRecipient must equal the argument passed by the caller; the bug sets it to address(0) regardless, so a subsequent call to getReward will transfer tokens to address(0) instead of the intended recipient, and rewardsRecipient() will return address(0) instead of the argument when the argument is non-zero.
After any call to setRewardsRecipient(x) by the owner, the contract's rewardsRecipient must equal the argument x; the bug stores msg.sender instead, so the invariant fails when the caller is not x.

After the owner calls setRewardsRecipient(address) with any argument, calling getReward(true) must not transfer tokens to any address other than the newly set rewardsRecipient; the bug sets rewardsRecipient to msg.sender, so when the original caller was not the argument, subsequent reward transfers go to the caller instead of the intended recipient.
After the owner calls setRewardsRecipient, rewardsRecipient must equal the argument _recipeint; the bug stores msg.sender instead, so re-reading rewardsRecipient differs.

After the owner calls setRewardsRecipient with any argument, a subsequent call to getReward by the operator must not move reward tokens to the original caller of setRewardsRecipient if that caller is not the operator; the bug stores msg.sender, so when the owner is not the operator, rewards are sent to the owner instead of the intended recipient.

After any sequence of calls to setRewardsRecipient by the owner, the value returned by rewardsRecipient() must equal the argument of the most recent such call; the bug stores msg.sender instead, so the rule fails when the caller is not the argument.
The return value of isCvxShutdown correctly reflects the shutdown status of the CVX booster pool, and the buggy inversion causes it to return the opposite boolean for any pool that is not shut down.

For any valid pool ID set via setCvxPoolInfo that has a defined shutdown status in the booster, isCvxShutdown() should return the same boolean as the booster's poolInfo(pId).shutdown; the buggy version inverts this, so for a pool that is not shut down the correct contract returns false while the buggy returns true.

For any valid pool ID and any shutdown state, isCvxShutdown() must return poolInfo(pId).shutdown; the bug inverts the boolean, so for a pool not shut down the reference returns false while the mutant returns true.
For any pool ID and any pool info in the booster, c.isCvxShutdown() must equal booster.poolInfo(pId).shutdown; the buggy mutant returns the inverted boolean.

For any pool, isCvxShutdown() must return booster.poolInfo(pId).shutdown; the mutant inverts it, so when the actual shutdown status is false, the reference returns false while the mutant returns true.
For any pool setup, `isCvxShutdown()` must equal the actual `shutdown` flag from the booster; the mutant always returns true, so it breaks when the pool is not shut down.
